title: cellquant: a single-script pipeline for quantitative fluorescence microscopy
description:
cellquant is a single-script command-line pipeline for quantitative multi-channel fluorescence microscopy. It performs cell and nuclear segmentation (Cellpose), puncta detection, per-cell intensity and condensation metrics, colocalization, and nucleolar proximity and morphology analysis, in either two or three dimensions.

The interface is entirely text based, so the exact command used to generate any result can be recorded and re-executed. It is designed for biologists who do not write code and who drive the tool through an AI assistant, and it refuses to run rather than produce a quietly-wrong number: a three-dimensional analysis with no known voxel size aborts instead of assuming isotropic 1 µm voxels, and colocalization on a maximum-intensity projection is refused unless explicitly forced, because collapsing the axial dimension inflates apparent overlap.

Accompanies the manuscript "Cellquant: a vibecoder's guide to image analysis". The raw image data underlying the published figures is archived separately; see the related identifiers below.
